title: Rising damp claimed by the surveyor — damp is at 1.5 m on a first-floor wall
why: The surveyor's hypothesis is rising damp. The evidence is a damp patch at roughly 1.5 m on a FIRST-FLOOR internal wall beside a bathroom — rising damp does not present there (playbook). The pipeline must disagree, not adopt the hypothesis.

room.name: Landing
room.note: Damp patch to wall shared with bathroom, about 1.5m up, roughly 40cm across. No tide mark low down, skirting dry. First floor.

transcripts: Landing, first floor, damp patch on the wall that backs onto the bathroom, it's about a metre and a half up, forty centimetres or so across. Skirting's dry, nothing low down. Forty two percent at the patch, twelve at skirting level. I'm going to put this down as rising damp.

must_not_happen.label: the pipeline must not agree with rising damp at 1.5 m on a first floor
rising damp is not the preferred cause
no external-fabric rows for an internal wall beside a bathroom

allowed_uncertainty: Preferred cause: penetrating damp from the bathroom (a leaking installation) or uncertain; the key is the explicit disagreement.
reviewer_notes: Readings: high at the patch, low at skirting — the profile is the opposite of rising damp.
